identity.title: DuQuant: Distributing Outliers via Dual Transformation Makes Stronger Quantized LLMs

problem.claim: Low-bit LLM quantization is hindered by outlier activations that are difficult to represent efficiently.

gap.claim: Existing approaches mainly handle normal outliers but struggle to smooth massive outliers, causing performance degradation in low-bit quantization.

contributions.claim: DuQuant combines block-wise rotation, zigzag permutation, and a subsequent rotation to mitigate both massive and normal outliers.
The authors report that DuQuant outperforms state-of-the-art baselines across LLM sizes and types, multiple tasks, and 4-bit weight-activation quantization.
The authors provide an implementation of DuQuant publicly.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe DuQuant as a novel rotation-and-permutation approach for mitigating both massive and normal outliers.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report superior performance to state-of-the-art baselines across various LLM sizes and types on multiple tasks, including 4-bit weight-activation quantization.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper identifies outlier activations as a major obstacle to efficient low-bit LLM quantization.
It distinguishes normal outliers from massive outliers and states that conventional methods primarily address the former.
DuQuant uses prior outlier dimensions to construct a block-wise rotation that redistributes outliers to adjacent channels.
A zigzag permutation balances outliers across blocks, reducing block-wise variance, followed by another rotation to smooth activations.
The authors report improved results over state-of-the-art baselines across model varieties, tasks, and 4-bit weight-activation quantization.

source_observation.claim: The abstract separates normal and massive outliers, then assigns distinct distribution-smoothing operations within a multi-stage transformation pipeline.

lessons.interpretation: A method can be framed more precisely when it maps distinct failure modes to explicit processing stages.
lessons.application: When presenting a quantization method, classify the problematic activation patterns first and explain which transformation addresses each pattern.
lessons.exception: This framing may be unsuitable when failure modes cannot be reliably distinguished or when the stages are not independently motivated.

unknowns: The abstract gives no numerical results, datasets, model names, baseline names, or experimental conditions.
It does not quantify the reduction in block-wise variance or specify how outlier dimensions are selected.
The abstract does not provide theoretical guarantees or implementation details beyond the code link.
